JOB SUMMARY: The Collections Operations Unit oversees residential waste collection programs and services, including garbage, recycling, organics, yard and leaf waste, for the city's designated collection zone, which currently serves 70,000 homes.

As a trainee, you will complete on-the-job training alongside a Waste Collection Operator (WCO) in order to learn the necessary skills to perform waste collection duties and responsibilities, safety and efficiently. Your duties and responsibilities (as outlined below) including operating vehicles and equipment and performing general labour in the collection and disposal of waste will gradually increase throughout the training and evaluation period.

Ontario Occupational Health & Safety Act (OHSA)
Understanding of mechanical and hydraulic systems to safely operate heavy equipment
Hazards, precautions, and safe operating practices for operating heavy equipment and vehicles
Proper lifting techniques
WHMIS, First Aid and Automated External Defibrillator (AED)
Knowledge of applicable health and safety legislation, including the rights and duties of workers

Read and follow route maps, drawings, and street signs
Understand and follow written and oral instructions
Able to successfully complete a Post-Offer Employment Test
Able to keep detailed, accurate records concerning materials received, processed, and disbursed as well as required equipment service records
Able to work collaboratively and take direction from staff while on assigned route
Understand and demonstrate safe working practices
Establish and maintain a good working relationship with management, other employees, and the public
Ability to communicate basic concepts to members of the public
Able to climb to and from the operator’s position and possess the manual dexterity and coordination to use both hands and feet simultaneously to operate a machine

Work in a variety of weather conditions with exposure to the outdoor elements

job_postings.title: Specialist, Child Care and Early Years Program Development and Support
job_postings.employment_type: Up to 1 Full-time Temporary position (Up to 1 Year)

JOB SUMMARY: You will be assigned to one of two portfolios, working as part of a team providing expert advice, guidance and input to program managers, and others who are responsible for the planning, management, implementation and evaluation of child care and early years programs and services in Ottawa.

You ensure the consistent planning, development, implementation, application and evaluation of a wide-range of child care and early years programs, policies and services; ensuring equitable access and inclusive, responsive and integrated programs and services for those who face barriers, manage complex projects; develop and advise on strategies; remain current on latest research related to Child Care and Early Childhood Development; and recommend and implement new programs and services, best practices and continuous improvement strategies.

You will lead or participate on committees and workgroups with community partners, government agencies, other City departments, and Children’s Services staff to plan, coordinate and strategize on issues to enhance access, affordability, quality and responsiveness of child care and early years programs and services, service delivery models, and innovative approaches to improvements to programs and deliverables. You will develop and manage contracts and monitor budgets to support program development and implementation.

You are responsible for implementation of child care and early years programs, policies, and services, including providing client-centric services through the innovation and management of technology, data analytics, financial and contract management, and reporting.

You will support the implementation of programs, policies and services; this includes providing technical expertise, consultation, and advice in the areas of project management, business analysis, financial and contract management, data management and analysis, process review and redesign, and the implementation of new/enhanced processes, technologies, applications and/or other solutions to meet Children’s Services business needs and improve client service delivery.
EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE: Completion of 4 year degree in Business Administration, Health Sciences, Social Sciences or related field

Minimum of 5 years of experience in child care, early years or related social services, health, education, recreation services related to children and/or youth, including experience in research, analysis, performance measurement, strategic and operational planning, policy development and program design, financial monitoring and budgeting, and contract management
KNOWLEDGE: Program design, development, implementation and evaluation
Planning, project and contract management techniques and methods including project management methodology
Stakeholder engagement mechanisms, approaches and communication strategies
Financial/ project or program budget management
Knowledge of the Child Care and Early Years Act. 2014 and related provincial and federal legislation
Child Care Programs and Early Childhood Education
Best practice approaches related to community and social services
Anti-racism and diversity, equity and inclusion principles and practices
Policy development and implementation
Partnership development (internal and external) including knowledge related specifically to the social services, health and recreation sectors.
Research and analysis methodology
Evaluation and quality improvement methodologies and techniques
Program design, development, implementation and evaluation
Anti-racism and diversity, equity and inclusion principles and practices
Knowledge of applicable health and safety legislation, including the rights and duties of workers.
COMPETENCIES, SKILLS AND ABILITIES: Client-service oriented dealing with City Staff, community groups and stakeholders
Team-player able to build strong working relationships internally and externally
Strong interpersonal skills to deliver presentations, facilitate discussions and negotiations, resolve conflict and communicate with both internal and external partners.
Conduct best-practice and operational reviews towards recommending service enhancements
Interpret and apply legislation to program strategy and development
Autonomous and able to manage own projects and time.
Consult on policy development and analysis, evaluation and best practices
Advanced computer skills and abilities in statistical modeling and data management utilizing Microsoft Office (EXCEL, POWERPOINT and WORD)
Manage multiple projects using project management techniques/skills
Organized, efficient, results-oriented, multi-tasker able to meet tight deadlines
Team-player able to build strong working relationships internally and
Innovative approach to service delivery strategies and problem solving
Advanced writing skills for presentations, policies, procedures, guidelines, program development and client/sector communications.
Advanced critical thinking skills and employs methodology and logic towards decision making.
WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW: Language Requirement: English oral, reading, writing
Experience and formal training combined with demonstrated performance and ability may substitute for stipulated academic requirements.
